system.name: BatchGen
system.one_liner: a system architecture for scalable and efficient batch inference of large language models

components.name: Global Batch
components.role: the full list of submitted sequences (..., Seq. 3, Seq. 2, Seq. 1) forming a batch inference job

components.name: Sub-Batch
components.role: a portion of the global batch processed and completed together, returning incremental output

components.name: BCT
components.role: batch completion time: total time from batch submission until every sequence has been processed

components.name: SCT
components.role: sequence completion time: time from batch submission until a specific sequence's output is available, set by its sub-batch's completion

components.name: Seq. 1
components.role: a single submitted sequence in the interactive inference panel

components.name: Submit
components.role: the user's submission action starting the interactive request timeline

components.name: TTFT
components.role: time to first token, measured from submission to the first output token

components.name: TPOT
components.role: time per output token, measured between successive output tokens

flows.what: sequences (e.g., Seq. 3) placed into a sub-batch for processing
all sub-batches together determine the total batch completion time
each sub-batch's completion determines the sequence completion time for its sequences
elapsed time until the first output token
elapsed time between subsequent output tokens

content.key_idea: Batch inference should be measured by batch completion time (BCT) and sequence completion time (SCT), which are fundamentally different from the per-token responsiveness metrics (TTFT, TPOT) used to evaluate interactive inference.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) Batch Inference read left to right along its time axis showing sub-batches and BCT/SCT brackets; right panel (b) Interactive Inference read left to right showing a submitted sequence's output tokens with TTFT/TPOT brackets.

palette.used_for: dark gray grid/hatch icons marking completed sub-batches and output-token squares
medium-light gray shading of elapsed sub-batch / TTFT-TPOT time bands
very light gray background shading of the timeline

style.font: HelveticaNeue sans-serif, 7-8pt, medium/bold for metric labels
style.arrows: straight double-headed bracket arrows measuring named time intervals
style.icons: vector; simple user/person icon, grid-hatch icon for completed batch, small squares for output tokens

encoding.color_means: dark gray = completed-work markers (grid squares for finished sub-batches, output-token squares), light gray shading = elapsed processing time bands along the time axis
encoding.line_style_means: double-headed arrow brackets measure named time intervals (BCT, SCT in panel a; TTFT, TPOT in panel b) directly against a shared time axis
encoding.emphasis: contrasts one long BCT bracket spanning the whole batch against multiple shorter per-sub-batch SCT brackets, versus TTFT/TPOT brackets for a single interactive sequence, motivating why batch inference needs different latency metrics
reusable_patterns: side-by-side timeline diagrams with bracket-style interval annotations to define and contrast latency metrics

evidence: As shown in Figure 1, we define the batch completion time (BCT) as the total time
SCT is determined by the completion time of the sub-batch that contains the sequence
interactive inference prioritizes user-perceived responsiveness, focusing on metrics such as time to first token

summary: This figure motivates BatchGen's design goals by contrasting batch inference with interactive inference along a shared time axis. Panel (a) Batch Inference shows a Global Batch of submitted sequences processed in Sub-Batches; it defines batch completion time (BCT) as the total time until every sequence in the batch is done, and sequence completion time (SCT) as the time until a specific sequence's sub-batch finishes and its output becomes available. Panel (b) Interactive Inference shows a single submitted sequence (Seq. 1) whose output tokens arrive over time, defining time to first token (TTFT) and time per output token (TPOT) as the relevant responsiveness metrics. The figure is a simple two-panel, flat grayscale timeline diagram with square-cornered blocks and double-headed bracket arrows labeling each interval, establishing that batch inference should optimize BCT/SCT rather than the token-level responsiveness metrics used for interactive inference.
summary_zh: 该图对比了批量推理与交互式推理的时间线：批量推理面板定义批完成时间（BCT）与序列完成时间（SCT），交互式推理面板定义首token时间（TTFT）与单token时间（TPOT），以此说明批量推理需要不同于交互式推理的评价指标，为 BatchGen 的设计目标提供动机。
